tools.name: effect.info
tools.description: Summarise a motion-graphics project (.ecproj) in the effect engine's workspace: its items with names, types, sizes, durations, and each composition's layer count and frame rate. Reads only. `path` is relative to that workspace, a private folder only the effect.* tools read and write; files elsewhere on the device are not in it and cannot be named.

tools.name: effect.render
tools.description: Render one frame of a composition (`comp`: its name or id, default the project's active one) at `time` seconds of a project in the effect engine's workspace, written as a PNG to `out` with its longest edge at most `max_side` pixels (default 1024); `transparent` keeps the alpha. Footage outside that workspace renders as a placeholder. Both paths are relative to that workspace (see effect.info); nothing is written outside it, and a file already at `out` is replaced.

tools.name: effect.export_lottie
tools.description: Export a composition (`comp`: its name or id) of a project in the effect engine's workspace as Lottie to `out` (.json, or .lottie for dotLottie), with the engine's warnings about what Lottie cannot carry; `include_expressions` keeps expressions. Both paths are relative to that workspace (see effect.info); nothing is written outside it, and a file already at `out` is replaced.

tools.name: effect.import_lottie
tools.description: Open a Lottie file (.json or .lottie) in the effect engine's workspace as a composition and save it as a project at `out` (.ecproj); embedded images are written beside the Lottie file. All paths are relative to that workspace (see effect.info); nothing is written outside it, and a file already at `out` is replaced.

tools.name: effect.run
tools.description: Run up to 64 commands from the effect engine's own command catalog, in order, on the project at `path` in the effect engine's workspace or on a new empty project, and save it to `out` when given. Each command is {id, params}. Plug-in loading is refused and the engine's file access stays inside that workspace. A generic engine command door: not granted to the system agent until it is reviewed separately.
